budgets.title: Free
budgets.cash: No new spend if you stay on a machine you have, or inside a provider's published always-free limit. Credits that expire are not this band.

budgets.title: Lab
budgets.cash: Cash stays at the hardware and power you already pay. No cloud account is required.

budgets.title: Standard
budgets.cash: Plan on a few hundred dollars a month for one isolated account, or less if the guests are small. This is a band, not an invoice.

budgets.title: Unlimited
budgets.cash: A dedicated account, packet capture, and every reserved org. Plan on four figures a month if the cloud side is real. The lab side costs power.

substrates.title: This machine
substrates.shape: Containers on one host you already have.

substrates.title: Proxmox
substrates.shape: Guests on a cluster you operate. The API address comes from the environment, never from this repo.

substrates.title: Google Cloud
substrates.shape: Free band: one e2-micro in us-west1, us-central1, or us-east1, with the published disk and egress caps. Larger bands pick their own private shape. No public address.

substrates.title: Oracle Cloud
substrates.shape: The published always-free Arm shape, if the tenancy still has it. That allowance has been cut before. Read the current card. Idle guests can be reclaimed. No public address.

substrates.title: AWS
substrates.shape: A private VPC and small guests. New accounts spend credits. There is no perpetual free host.
substrates.expires: AWS credits end. When they end, this account bills. It is not the free band.

substrates.title: Azure
substrates.shape: A private network and a small burstable guest. The introductory VM hours and the signup credit both end.
substrates.expires: Azure's introductory allowance ends. It is not the free band.

substrates.title: Lab plus private cloud
substrates.shape: The habitat stays on Proxmox. A second private network holds a sensor replica. No public address and no path to the real internet.

windows.title: No Windows
windows.note: Samba, FreeIPA, Keycloak, Authentik, OpenLDAP, step-ca, RADIUS. No AD CS.

windows.title: Evaluation media you supply
windows.note: You obtain the image from Microsoft. This repo never stores it.

windows.title: Your license
windows.note: Your agreement, your key, kept out of this repo.

densities.title: Smoke
densities.note: Northline's logical hosts, collapsed onto one guest.

densities.title: Living
densities.note: Directory, apps, and sensors on separate guests. One org, unless the band allows a second.

densities.title: Federation
densities.note: Every selected org gets a block. The harness scope does not open those blocks until a later compile.

identity.title: Directory record
identity.note: The catalog of accounts. Always on. Not a network service.

identity.title: Samba directory
identity.note: A Linux directory. No Microsoft license. Not a stand-in for certificate services.

identity.title: Windows directory
identity.note: A real directory on media you supply. One forest for the org. No trust in this phase.

identity.title: Certificate enrollment
identity.note: One loose template class. The catalog names the class. It does not say how to use it.

identity.title: Missing local-admin rotation
identity.note: The abandoned patch cohort does not rotate local admin. The material stays in the seed vault.

identity.title: Keycloak
identity.note: Staff portal in front of the first-party apps. A loose partner client is a class, not a procedure.

identity.title: Authentik
identity.note: A second portal style. Pick this or Keycloak unless two departments really have two portals.

identity.title: FreeIPA
identity.note: Realm for the Linux servers. Hosts join it. The harness does not get the enrollment material.

identity.title: OpenLDAP
identity.note: An application directory for a system that should not be on the staff domain.

identity.title: step-ca
identity.note: Internal enrollment when there is no Windows certificate service.

identity.title: Standalone Kerberos
identity.note: A KDC without a full directory. Redundant if Samba or Windows is already selected.

identity.title: RADIUS
identity.note: Network devices ask a local server. The shared secret stays in the vault.

identity.title: Partner broker
identity.note: A separate portal for the vendor extranet. Not a forest trust.

detection.title: Zeek
detection.note: Network metadata on a span. The span sits on the management plane.

detection.title: Suricata
detection.note: Alerts on the same span. Rules describe classes, not how to use a weakness.

detection.title: Wazuh
detection.note: Host agents report to a manager the harness is not allowed to reach.

detection.title: OpenSearch
detection.note: Search for the SOC. The lighter choice when Elastic is more than the band can hold.

detection.title: Elastic
detection.note: Search for the SOC. Heavier than OpenSearch. Not a fit for an always-free guest.

detection.title: Velociraptor
detection.note: Endpoint questions from the management plane.

detection.title: osquery
detection.note: Scheduled endpoint questions. Fleet manages them when you add it.

detection.title: Fleet
detection.note: Manages osquery. Needs osquery, and needs more than an always-free guest.

detection.title: Sigma
detection.note: Detection classes only. The files do not describe how to use a weakness.

detection.title: TheHive
detection.note: Cases for the night analyst. Not a feed from the public internet.

detection.title: MISP
detection.note: Synthetic events seeded in the lab. No outbound feed.

detection.title: Arkime
detection.note: Packet capture. Disk-heavy. Management plane only.

bundles.title: Security Onion
bundles.note: A bundle of Zeek, Suricata, and Elastic. It counts as those three, and it does not fit the free band.

noise.title: Caldera noise floor
noise.note: Background noise so a quiet range is not a tell. Reaching it means the harness already left scope.

noise.title: OpenAEV noise
noise.note: Seeded exercise traffic on the management plane. Not a harness, and not a procedure.
